title: An informal letter
subtitle: Answering your friend's news
goal: You can answer a friend's letter: react to their news, tell your own, ask two questions and close warmly.
why: An informal letter is the most tested A2 genre — and the one where students forget to answer the questions they were asked.
example: Aliya answered a pen-friend's letter point by point. Her partner wrote: 'you are the only one who answered everything'.
writeTask: Answer a letter from your friend (60–90 words): thank them, react to their news, tell two pieces of your own news, ask two questions and close warmly.

tasks.title: Build the sentence
tasks.howto: Tap the words in the right order — they move into the line. Tap a word in the line to send it back. English word order is fixed, so the order itself carries the meaning.

items.src: This café is good. That café is not so good.
answers: This café is better than that one.
items.why: A comparison needs the comparative form plus than.

answers: I will come at half past seven.
items.why: Later means nothing to the reader; a time does.

items.cue: Add an adjective and a detail
answers: It was a small wooden house near the river.
items.why: One adjective and one place detail change a bare sentence into a picture.

items.src: I will visit my aunt next week. It is my plan.
answers: I am going to visit my aunt next week.
items.why: Going to is for plans you have already made.

items.src: The film was boring, because I left.
answers: The film was boring, so I left.
items.why: Because gives the reason, so gives the result. They face opposite ways.

items.src: I was late. The bus did not come.
answers: I was late because the bus did not come.
items.why: Because turns two short sentences into one clear idea.
Experience up to now takes Present Perfect: I have never visited.

answers: Could you send me the photos, please?
items.why: Could you…? turns an order into a request.

tasks.title: Rewrite it

items.after: , I had to work on Saturday.

items.before: The café was small and noisy.

But joins a good point and a bad point in one sentence.

items.before: We booked the tickets in May

Also adds one more reason to like it.

rules.msg: The opening line names the subject: a reader who does not know the topic stops after one sentence.
The closing part sums up or asks — it never introduces a new fact.

tasks.title: Write it step by step
tasks.howto: Answer one question at a time, in English, one or two sentences. At the end your answers become a draft in the Writing Pad. The hints are questions, not ready sentences: the text stays yours.

tasks.prompt: Answer a letter from your friend (60–90 words): thank them, react to their news, tell two pieces of your own news, ask two questions and close warmly.
tasks.title: Your own text
tasks.howto: Now the whole text, on your own. The Writing Pad gives you the checklist, the phrase bank, the linking words and your plan. The timer is optional.
